name: PlanetScale
tagline: Performance-focused managed MySQL (Vitess) and Postgres, with NVMe-backed Metal clusters and branching.
description: PlanetScale is a managed database company built by core Vitess maintainers. It started with Vitess-based MySQL, adding schema branches and deploy requests for safe, non-blocking migrations, and in 2025 launched PlanetScale Postgres, followed by Neki, its own sharding layer for Postgres. Metal clusters run on local NVMe drives instead of network storage, trading elastic disks for much lower and steadier latency. The hobby free tier is gone; the entry point is now a $5 single-node Postgres, and production clusters are priced per primary-plus-two-replicas. Choose it when you care about tail latency, zero-downtime schema changes and a credible path to sharding, rather than scale-to-zero pricing.

pricing.notes: HA Postgres from $15/month, Metal Postgres from $50/month, Vitess from $39/month; Neki shards from $30/month plus routers. Storage, backups and egress extra.

scale.notes: Vitess databases shard horizontally today; Postgres scales vertically with replicas, with Neki providing sharding; cross-region read replicas available.

strengths: Metal clusters on local NVMe give low, predictable query latency
Schema branches and deploy requests make migrations reviewable and non-blocking
Battle-tested Vitess sharding for MySQL at very large scale
Both MySQL and Postgres under one control plane
Query Insights surfaces slow queries and index recommendations
weaknesses: No free tier since 2024; even hobby use is paid
Vitess-based MySQL restricts some features (e.g. foreign keys were long unsupported)
No scale-to-zero; you pay for provisioned clusters
Postgres sharding (Neki) is new and less proven than Vitess
useCases: High-traffic SaaS backends sensitive to tail latency
Teams that want safe, reviewable schema changes in CI
Migrating from RDS/Aurora to faster NVMe-backed Postgres
notIdealFor: Spiky workloads that benefit from scale-to-zero
